title: [Epic] E2E Stability — Post-2026.q1.11-lts Run Failure Resolution
body:
## Description

First successful full E2E run on `2026.q1.11-lts` completed on Jul 26, 2026 with 138 passed and 252 failed. LPD-91054 auto-deploy bug is confirmed fixed (27/27 collections, 129 fragments deployed). This epic tracks resolution of the remaining 252 failures across three root-cause groups.

## Analysis

All 252 failures share the symptom `Fragment 'X' was not found on the page (selector: div[id^="fragment-"] returned 0 elements)`. Root causes fall into three groups:

- **Group A**: Object definition batch CX extensions hadn't finished registering before `global-setup.js` created pages (9 object ERCs affected)
- **Group B**: ~200 fragments render blank — sub-causes include cascading object dependency failures, container fragments needing child content, selector mismatches, and rendering timeouts
- **Infrastructure**: Docker volumes for OSGi state created with `root:root` ownership preventing Liferay's uid 1000 process from writing

## Implementation Plan

1. Fix volume permissions in `test-runner.sh` (Phase 2)
2. Increase object definition retry timing in `global-setup.js` (Phase 1)
3. Investigate and fix fragment DOM selector for Group B (Phase 3)
4. Commit E2E results and close LPD-91054

issues.title: Fix: Pre-chmod Docker volumes before ldm run to prevent OSGi lock crash
issues.body:
## Description

When `ldm run` creates the `e2e-test-env-state` and `e2e-test-env-data` Docker volumes for the first time, they are initialised with `root:root` ownership and `0755` permissions. Liferay runs as uid 1000 (non-root) and cannot write to these directories, causing the OSGi `StorageManager` to fail immediately with `java.io.IOException: Unable to create lock manager`.

This crash occurs on every fresh environment boot without a manual workaround.

## Analysis

The volumes are declared as `external: true` in the generated `docker-compose.yml`. Docker initialises new named volumes owned by root. The Liferay container user (uid 1000) needs write access to `/opt/liferay/osgi/state` and `/opt/liferay/data` to boot successfully.

Current manual workaround:
```bash
docker run --rm -v e2e-test-env-state:/state -v e2e-test-env-data:/data alpine sh -c "chmod 777 /state /data"
```

This workaround is lost on every `/tmp` clear (e.g. server restart) and must be re-applied manually.

## Implementation Plan

1. In `scripts/test-runner.sh`, add a pre-`ldm run` step that uses an Alpine container to `chmod 777` the `e2e-test-env-state` and `e2e-test-env-data` volumes
2. Guard the step so it only runs when not in skip-deploy mode
3. Log the step clearly for visibility
4. Separately raise with LDM team to fix volume initialisation ownership upstream

issues.title: Fix: Increase object definition retry timeout in global-setup.js
issues.body:
## Description

During the E2E run on `2026.q1.11-lts`, 9 custom Liferay Object definitions (APPLICANT, TICKET, TICKET_COMMENT, CAMPAIGN, AUDIT_ENTRY, HEART_RATE, BLOOD_PRESSURE, STEPS, WEIGHT) had not finished registering when `global-setup.js` began creating test pages. Fragments depending on these objects rendered blank, causing ~50 test failures.

## Analysis

The batch client extension object definitions are deployed asynchronously. The current retry loop polls 5 attempts × 3s = 15s maximum wait. On a fresh Liferay boot, object registration takes longer than 15s.

Affected fragments include: Listbox Multiselect, Image Choice, Address Autocomplete, Autocomplete (Object/Picklist), Confirmation Field, Comment, View Comments, Audit Button, Campaign Insights, Campaign Initialiser, Activity Heatmap, Meter Reading.

## Implementation Plan

1. In `e2e-tests/tests/global-setup.js`, increase the object definition retry loop from `5 attempts × 3s` to `15 attempts × 5s` (75s maximum wait)
2. Add a global pre-check gate that waits for ALL required object definitions to be registered before creating any test pages
3. Log which objects are still pending at each retry attempt for diagnostics

issues.title: Investigate: Fragment not found in DOM for ~200 fragments on 2026.q1.11-lts
issues.body:
## Description

After the E2E run on `2026.q1.11-lts`, approximately 200 fragments fail with `Fragment 'X' was not found on the page (selector: div[id^="fragment-"] returned 0 elements)`. Pages were created successfully by global-setup but the fragment DOM element is absent when Playwright inspects the page.

## Analysis

Possible sub-causes:
- **B1**: Cascade from object definition timing failures (Group A) — fragments that require an object render blank if the object wasn't registered when the page was created
- **B2**: Container fragments (Dashboard Container, Overlay Background, Linear Gradient Container) require child content to render their wrapper element
- **B3**: Fragment selector `div[id^="fragment-"]` may not match all fragment types, particularly widget-modifier fragments (Back Button, Icon Button, Pulse Button) which may use a different DOM structure
- **B4**: Rendering timeout — heavy API-calling fragments may not have finished rendering within the current `networkidle` wait

## Implementation Plan

1. After Phase 1 (object timing fix), re-run full E2E suite to identify remaining failures with Group A resolved
2. Pick 3 representative failing fragments (gemini-generated, form-fragment, widget-modifier) and run with Playwright `--debug` to inspect actual DOM
3. Add configurable `verificationSelector` field to `test-data.json` schema, falling back to the broad selector if not specified
4. For container fragments: evaluate whether to add child content in `test-data.json` or mark `excludeFromGallery: true`
5. Update `fragments.spec.js` to use per-fragment verification selector
